headline: Freight squalls and a Section 232 pressure front are converging over equipment purchasing.
dek: W26 is not one storm. It is a clock collision: freight rates, tariff classifications, fuel-linked surcharges, port timing, inventory cost and supplier proof all move on different calendars.

zones.name: Freight lanes
zones.operator_meaning: Drewry WCI rose 5% to $4,166/40ft; Shanghai-LA hit $5,750 and Shanghai-NY $7,149, so the price of waiting increased again.
zones.watch: Next Drewry/Freightos prints after July GRIs and peak-season surcharges.

zones.name: Equipment BOMs
zones.operator_meaning: Steel, aluminum and copper derivative treatment now turns SKU economics into HTS classification, origin, metal-content and supplier-evidence work.
zones.watch: CBP/Commerce guidance, annex coverage, USMCA treatment and attestation requirements.

zones.name: Inventory placement
zones.operator_meaning: LMI Inventory Costs around 84 and Transportation Prices at 96.0 mean pull-forward decisions carry local cost even when annual logistics-cost narratives look calmer.
zones.watch: Overflow quotes, receiving labor, and whether inventory is a demand bet or a tariff hedge.

zones.name: Retail ports
zones.operator_meaning: NRF/Hackett sees June imports at 2.25M TEU, up 14.3% YoY, then negative YoY readings from July through September; port strength may be frontloading, not demand quality.
zones.watch: July-September import forecast revisions and retailer commentary on margin/inventory.

zones.name: Strategic inputs
zones.operator_meaning: China's export-control/procurement lists keep strategic-input risk alive, but this is a watch item because mine-to-battery ran recently.
zones.watch: Any move from symbolic defense-linked listings into commercial industrial inputs.

reference_cards.label: Drewry WCI
reference_cards.note: +5% WoW on 25 Jun; highest Drewry reports since Sep 2024.

reference_cards.label: Shanghai-LA
reference_cards.note: +12% WoW; Transpacific did most of the visible work.

reference_cards.label: LMI cost stack
reference_cards.note: Inventory Costs ~84; Transportation Prices 96.0; Transportation Capacity 31.7.

reference_cards.label: NRF June imports
reference_cards.note: +14.3% YoY, followed by negative YoY forecasts July-Sep.

reference_cards.label: Section 232 bands
reference_cards.note: Treatment depends on category, content, origin, annexes and proof.

operator_watchlist: Do not blend Drewry, LMI, NRF and port data into a fake master index; they are separate weather stations.
For equipment POs, make item-master evidence the first workstream: HTS, metal content, origin, annex mapping, supplier attestation.
Treat strong port/import numbers as possible frontloading until demand evidence agrees.
Book warehouse space/labor before approving pull-forward freight; receiving capacity is part of the forecast.
Keep rare earths in What to Watch unless controls spread into broader commercial industrial inputs.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: Transpacific squalls meet a Section 232 pressure front.
newsletter_insert.body: This week's operating weather is a clock collision, not a single headline. Freight rates are moving now, tariff evidence has to be ready before the purchase order, and import strength may be frontloading rather than demand confidence.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: If `ore to equipment` wins Sunday, the job is not to forecast metal prices. It is to decide which equipment SKUs need HTS/content/origin proof before the freight and policy clocks close.
